name: Godot 4.7.2 headless-container lighting probe (Vulkan Forward+ on lavapipe, real Aokigahara data)
environment_steps:
Resumed from an earlier partial attempt that had already downloaded and extracted Godot_v4.7.2-stable_linux.x86_64 (4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, the latest stable release, 18 Aug 2026) from the GitHub release assets and had installed mesa-vulkan-drivers. I moved the binary into proto/godot/bin/ and deleted the 78 MB godot.zip. Xvfb was already installed.
1) apt-get install -y mesa-vulkan-drivers   (lavapipe; this also upgraded mesa-libgallium, libgl1-mesa-dri and libgbm1 to 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.2)
2) Project written entirely as text files, with no editor and no import step (no .godot/ folder is ever created): proj/project.godot, proj/main.tscn (a single Node3D with a script) and proj/main.gd (about 520 lines of GDScript that builds everything at runtime).
3) Render command (Forward+ worked first time; I did not need to fall back to mobile or gl_compatibility):
   cd .../scratchpad/proto/godot && xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x800x24" bin/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_linux.x86_64 --path proj --rendering-driver vulkan --rendering-method forward_plus --resolution 1280x800 -- --mode=sdfgi|nosdfgi|canopy|sdfgi_canopy --frames=30 [--sun_energy=6.0 --tag=name]
   The log reports: "Vulkan 1.4.318 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: Unknown - llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits)".
   Batch runner: proto/godot/run_all.sh (renders the sdfgi, nosdfgi and canopy frames in sequence and logs wall times to logs/wall.txt).
4) Scoring: python3 /home/user/Aokigahara/tools/lighting_stats.py out/godot_*.png --json out/lighting_stats_godot.json
What the script does at runtime:
- Reads local-height.f32 and its json (257x257, 8 m, y = elevation - 900) into an ArrayMesh with computed normals, plus a UV2 channel for the canopy map.
- Applies a StandardMaterial3D with world triplanar mapping, using moss diff, nor_gl and rough images loaded with Image.load_from_file.
- Loads tree-library-v2.glb through GLTFDocument and GLTFState and finds meshes by name (tsuga/hinoki high, low and far LODs, snags, saplings, rocks, logs).
- Places trees with MultiMeshInstance3D:
  - 8,925 real placements from forest-instances.f32 within 480 m (high LOD under 32 m, low under 220 m, far beyond);
  - 1,897 procedural sub-canopy stems on a 5 m jittered grid within 160 m;
  - 597 saplings, rocks and logs within 55 m;
  - 34 multimeshes and 5.0 M instance triangles in total.
- Lighting:
  - sun at 24° elevation from WSW, 4-split PSSM, 150 m shadow distance, light_angular_distance 0.6 (soft shadows), 4096 atlas;
  - PhysicalSkyMaterial, AgX tonemapping, auto-exposure through CameraAttributesPractical;
  - SSAO, SSIL, SDFGI (4 cascades, occlusion on, reads sky light), volumetric fog plus exponential depth fog, glow, TAA; foliage backlight turned on.
- Captures with get_viewport().get_texture().get_image().save_png, writes a JSON stats file and quits.
- Canopy trick: every crown is splatted into a 2 m/px cover map over the whole 2 km terrain, box-averaged to 8 m and turned into sky visibility = exp(-1.6*cover). This is applied to the ground material as an AO texture on UV2 with ao_light_affect 0, so it darkens only ambient, sky and GI light. It takes 80 ms and is saved as out/canopy_sky_visibility.png.
The repository was not modified. It shows one untracked file, wicked_features.txt, which I did not create.
what_worked: Godot 4.7.2 rendered in the GPU-less container using Forward+ over software Vulkan (lavapipe/llvmpipe, Vulkan 1.4.318) under xvfb-run. The first renderer tried worked, so I never needed mobile or gl_compatibility.

The whole project is three hand-written text files and needs no editor import step. Runtime loading of the repository's real data worked: the DEM .f32 went into an ArrayMesh, the JPEG textures loaded via Image.load_from_file, tree-library-v2.glb loaded via GLTFDocument and GLTFState (all 37 meshes found by name), and forest-instances.f32 fed the MultiMeshes.

Every Forward+ lighting feature I asked for ran on lavapipe without errors: SDFGI (occlusion on, sky light read), SSAO, SSIL, volumetric fog, PSSM 4-split soft directional shadows, PhysicalSky, AgX, auto-exposure, glow and TAA. The only log errors were the harmless ALSA/PulseAudio fallback to the dummy audio driver.
Scores against the UE5.8 g–j targets (sunfleck 0.07–0.16, shadow_blue 1.16–1.73, log_avg 0.003–0.008, stops 8.5–10):

SDFGI on: log_avg 0.0056 (in range), stops 8.02 (below range), sunfleck 0.158 (in range), shadow_blue 1.23 (in range). Meets 3 of 4 and is the closest to the valued UE look: the understorey is dark and sky-occluded with dappled sunflecks on the floor.

SDFGI off: log_avg 0.0106 (outside), stops 6.46 (outside), sunfleck 0.083 (in range), shadow_blue 1.07 (outside). Meets 1 of 4: the floor is flat and too bright because unoccluded sky ambient fills the shadows.

SDFGI off with the canopy sky-visibility AO trick: log_avg 0.0064 (in range), stops 6.64 (outside), sunfleck 0.126 (in range), shadow_blue 1.05 (outside). Meets 2 of 4. The 80 ms trick recovers most of SDFGI's floor darkening and sunfleck contrast. It does not bring back the cool, blue-sky tint in the shadows, and it does not darken trunks or rocks because only the ground material uses it.

SDFGI plus the canopy trick with sun energy 6: log_avg 0.0078 (in range), stops 7.93 (outside), sunfleck 0.163 (just over 0.16), shadow_blue 1.11 (outside). Meets 1 of 4. Adding the canopy AO on top of SDFGI removes blue sky light from the shadows, so this combination is a step back.
Timing:
Scene build takes 0.7–1.2 s.
The first rendered frame takes about 25 s (pipeline compilation plus SDFGI initialisation).
Steady state at 1280x800 with 5.0 M instance triangles is 7.4 s/frame with SDFGI, 6.2 s/frame without SDFGI, 6.8 s/frame with the canopy trick, and 4.9 s/frame for the SDFGI + canopy run.
Wall time per captured frame is 253 s (SDFGI, 30 frames), 167 s (no SDFGI, 24 frames), 189 s (canopy, 24 frames) and 192 s (SDFGI + canopy, 30 frames).
About 13.5 min of rendering produced the 4 final frames. With the two smoke tests and the time spent writing the project, the whole task took roughly 45–50 min.
My first smoke test, with 8.3 M triangles, an 8192 shadow atlas and higher soft-shadow quality, ran at 24.7 s/frame. Cutting it down to 5 M triangles and a 4096 atlas brought it to about 7 s/frame.
Disk use:
Godot binary: 140 MB extracted (the 78 MB zip has been deleted).
mesa-vulkan-drivers: 96 MB installed. mesa-libgallium (42 MB) was already present and only upgraded; Xvfb was preinstalled (2 MB).
Godot and Mesa shader and user caches: about 17 MB (~/.local/share/godot 8.7 MB, ~/.cache/godot 3.2 MB, ~/.cache/mesa_shader_cache 5.4 MB).
Project: 36 KB. Outputs: 6.4 MB.
The agent loop works: I read each PNG back, scored it with tools/lighting_stats.py, tuned exposure, density, fog and camera, and re-rendered, all inside the container.
blockers: Iteration is slow on the CPU renderer: about 3–4 minutes per settled frame, and about 25 s of pipeline compilation on every launch. Tuning several parameters means many multi-minute runs.

Dynamic range stayed at about 8.0 stops against the 8.5–10 target. The sky gaps render as a dull grey-blue rather than bright near-white, and sunflecks are greener and less warm and saturated than in UE frames g–j. I did not have time to tune the sky energy, sun colour and moss albedo further.

There are no distinct light shafts. Volumetric fog only adds a general haze towards the sun side. Shafts would need tuning of fog density against froxel volume size, or FogVolumes, which I did not try.

The canopy is only moderately dense. The GLB crowns are sparse fir-spray cards, so I had to add procedural sub-canopy stems (the three.js viewer also does this) before the floor was shaded enough. The canopy trick darkens only the terrain: trunks, rocks and foliage keep full sky ambient.

Lavapipe is a correctness and appearance check, not a performance proxy. The frame times say nothing about the M2 Air. SDFGI through Godot's Metal driver on the Mac could also look different, since the earlier research noted a Metal-specific SDFGI bounce bug.

The first frame of each run can include partly converged SDFGI or TAA history. I waited 24–30 frames. Because frames are slow, auto-exposure converges almost immediately, but its behaviour at a real 60 fps has not been checked.
The repository has an untracked file, wicked_features.txt, which I did not create; another agent presumably did. I left it alone.
implications:
It works: an agent in a Linux cloud container with no GPU and 4 CPUs can write a Godot 4.7.2 project from scratch, run it on the repository's real terrain, trees and materials through the real Forward+ renderer (SDFGI, SSIL, volumetric fog and soft PSSM shadows included), capture 1280x800 PNGs, and score them against the UE5.8 baseline. The owner's Mac is not needed for any of it. The added setup is about 240 MB on disk: a 140 MB binary and 96 MB of Mesa. There is no editor, no import cache and no derived data cache.

On the owner's main criterion, the forest lighting, SDFGI clearly matters. With it on, the frame meets 3 of the 4 UE5.8 g–j targets (exposure key, sunfleck fraction and cool shadows) and just misses dynamic range, at 8.0 stops against 8.5. With it off, the frame meets 1 of 4. The cheap canopy sky-visibility map, which could equally be baked from the LiDAR canopy height model, recovers most of the floor darkening at no runtime cost and meets 2 of 4. It does not bring back the sky-blue shadows, so it suits distant or low-end areas better than replacing GI. By eye the SDFGI frame reads as a plausible sky-occluded conifer interior with dappled sun. It is not yet at the level of Lumen: the sky gaps are dull, there are no shafts, and the sunflecks are less warm.

For the workflow, this makes Godot practical as a self-verifying render target:
- Keep scenes as text and GDScript.
- Render stills with the command above, one mode per run, waiting 24–30 frames.
- Put lighting_stats.py plus a contact sheet into each agent iteration as a regression gate.
- Budget about 4 minutes per settled frame, so choose viewpoints deliberately rather than sweeping many.
- Save the owner's Mac for performance checks and for confirming that the same scene looks the same through Metal.
Next tuning steps:
- For range and sky gaps: raise sky energy and exposure clamping, and make sunlit albedo warmer.
- For shafts: add FogVolumes or denser volumetric fog.
- Apply the canopy visibility to trunks and foliage through a ShaderMaterial or instance data.
disk_used: Godot 4.7.2 binary 140 MB (zip deleted); mesa-vulkan-drivers 96 MB (plus mesa-libgallium 42 MB, already present and only upgraded); Xvfb preinstalled (2 MB); Godot and Mesa caches ~17 MB; project 36 KB; renders and logs ~6.5 MB. Added in total: about 255 MB.
timings:
All runs use Vulkan Forward+ on lavapipe (llvmpipe, LLVM 20.1.2, 4 CPUs) at 1280x800 with 5.0 M instance triangles.
- Scene build: 0.7–1.2 s.
- First rendered frame: about 25 s (pipeline compilation plus SDFGI initialisation).
- Steady state: 7.4 s/frame with SDFGI, 6.2 s/frame without SDFGI, 6.8 s/frame with the canopy trick, 4.9 s/frame for SDFGI + canopy.
- Wall time per captured frame: sdfgi (30 frames) 253 s, nosdfgi (24) 167 s, canopy (24) 189 s, sdfgi_canopy_sun6 (30) 192 s.
- Smoke tests: 8.3 M triangles with an 8192 shadow atlas ran at 24.7 s/frame (149 s wall for 5 frames); after cutting down to 5 M triangles and a 4096 atlas it ran at about 7.7 s/frame.
- Rendering all 4 final frames took about 13.5 min. The whole task took about 45–50 min.
versions: Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf (Linux x86_64 editor binary from the GitHub release assets); Mesa 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.2 (lavapipe, llvmpipe LLVM 20.1.2, Vulkan 1.4.318); Vulkan loader 1.3.275; Xvfb 21.1.12 (Ubuntu 24.04); Python numpy 2.4.6 and Pillow 12.3.0 for scoring.
